title: Ops-tribe SLO activation marathon plan - 2026
content:
Purpose

This is a working plan for an intensive cross-functional SLO activation "marathon" across Ops, Platform, Product, and Feature tribes. The goal is to run a tightly timeboxed program (6 weeks) that moves a set of pilot services from informal uptime/latency practices to measured, tested, and actionable SLOs with clear error-budget workflows. This doc is intentionally tactical and biased toward quick experiments + learning.

Scope and outcomes (what success looks like)
- Scope: 4 pilot services (one from Hosted API, one from Dedicated control plane, one from Console, one infra tooling)
- Outcomes: published SLOs + dashboards, automated alerting tied to error budget burn policies, one canary rollback policy per service, documented runbooks and a short post-mortem template, 2 quantitative learnings on batching/cache effects on latency and cost
- Success metrics: 90% of owners have run at least one error-budget-driven action in the window; two incidents simulated and resolved using new runbooks; average time-to-detect reduced 30% on pilot paths

Program structure (6-week marathon)
- Week 0 (Preparation, parallel): stakeholder kickoff, data access, traffic sampling, confirm SLIs and measurement sources.
- Week 1-2 (Ignition): formalize SLIs, set initial SLO targets, baseline dashboards, short risk/impact mapping. Run quick query experiments to validate metric fidelity.
- Week 3-4 (Relay): implement alerting + error budget policies, run a small canary rollout for model/infra variant, begin failure injection mini-sprints (non-prod).
- Week 5 (Taper): execute controlled live canary on low-risk path, finalize runbooks, train on-call and product owners. Collect retrospective data.
- Week 6 (Harvest): post-mortem + org sync, decide next-phase (scale to more services, change SLO targets, automation backlog).

Roles & responsibilities (quick roster)
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (eng-sre) - overall schedule, escalation, stakeholder liaison
- Metrics & dashboards: Evan Chen (observability) - create baseline dashboards + signal sanity checks
- Alerting + automation: Priya Mehta (platform-engineering) - implement alerting rules + hooks to error-budget workflows
- Failure injection & chaos: Lars Olsen (serving-runtime) - coordinate experiments and safety gates
- Product & UX liaison: Maya Gupta (product-hosted-api) - communicate impact, own customer-visible SLA language
- Runbook author: Noah Brooks (site-reliability-engineering) - consolidate runbooks and incident scripts

Minimum viable SLO template (to be filled per service)
- Service: <service-name>
- SLI(s): p95 request latency (app-level), availability success-rate (5xx and client-visible errors), queue length/backlog for async workers
- Measurement window: rolling 30d for availability, rolling 7d for latency experiments
- Initial SLO target: availability 99.9% (subject to historical baseline), p95 latency target based on 75th percentile of current traffic
- Error budget policy: soft alerts at 30% burn, page at 70% burn in 7d window, org review at 100% burn
- Response actions: incremental throttling, temporary scaling, traffic routing to standby region, manual rollback for canary variant

Data plan & sampling notes
- Data owners: telemetry is in observability cluster X, trace sampling at 10% for model calls to reduce cost during the marathon
- Metric validation checklist: continuity (no gaps), cardinality sanity, alignment between traced requests and metrics; run reconciliation queries week 0
- Cheap experiments: prefix caching on edge for small subset of requests to measure latency delta before applying broad rollout

Alerting & error-budget automation (practical rules)
- Use tagging convention: team:ops-tribe, slo-pilot:true on alerts generated from these SLOs
- Alert channel: #sre-ops-activation-thread; pages only when policy hit AND cross-check probe verifies degraded state
- Automations: webhook to /internal/error-budget/action with payload {service, policy, action} (Priya to own)

Canary & fallback pattern (a 'canary of canaries')
- Canary steps: warm baseline -> 1% traffic for 1 hour -> 5% for 4 hours -> 25% for 12 hours -> 100% ramp if no SLO regressions
- Stop conditions: sustained p95 above threshold for 30m, availability drop >0.2% absolute, unexplained error spike >x3 baseline
- Fallbacks: immediate routing to previous stable variant, automated rollback on deployment platform, incident bridge with owners pinged

Risk register (top risks & mitigations)
- Measurement drift: mitigation: week 0 reconciliation + synthetic probes as a canary
- Alert fatigue: mitigation: use soft alerts + consolidate noise; require multi-signal confirmation before paging
- Customer impact during canary: mitigation: schedule low-traffic windows; route test traffic when possible; have clear rollback plan
- Insufficient instrumentation: mitigation: triage tickets for infra owners and postpone canary until minimum fidelity met

Meeting cadence & artifacts
- Weekly program sync (Mon 11am, 30m) - status + blockers
- Fast standup (Tue/Thu 15m) during Relay weeks for rollout coordination
- War-room template: short link to "ops-activation/war-room-template" (Confluence)
- Key artifacts: baseline dashboard, SLO definition doc per service, runbooks, canary checklist, post-mortem template

Action list (first 10-day backlog)
- Day 1: Kickoff, confirm owners + access (Aisha)
- Day 2-3: Metrics instrumentation audit (Evan)
- Day 4: Draft SLO targets per service (owners + product)
- Day 5: Create baseline dashboards and signal sanity checks (Evan)
- Day 6-8: Implement alerting hooks + error-budget webhook (Priya)
- Day 9-10: Failure injection rehearsal in staging (Lars)

Notes to self / open questions
- How conservative should initial SLOs be vs aiming for stretch targets? Recommend start conservative to avoid unwarranted org churn.
- Do we need legal/comms sign-off for customer-facing SLA text? Check with product (Maya) week 1.
- Consider running a short survey with on-call engineers to capture existing pain points we can prioritize.

Retrospective & learning capture (post-marathon)
- 2-page summary: What went well, what blocked us, three clear improvements for next cohort
- Quantitative appendix: A/B results for caching/batching changes, error budget burn curves, MTTR pre/post
- Decision log: whether to promote patterns to org-wide defaults or keep experimental

Appendix: quick templates (copy/paste)
- SLO definition (one-liner): "<service> will achieve X% availability measured over 30d rolling windows for production traffic"
- Runbook stub: Symptoms -> Verification steps -> Mitigation -> Post-incident actions -> Owner

End — this is an iterative draft. Please add inline comments, link tickets, and tag changes with reviewer initials.

Jira starter tickets to create: ENG-SLO-0001 (baseline dashboards), ENG-SLO-0002 (alerting hooks), ENG-SLO-0003 (canary checklist), ENG-SLO-0004 (post-mortem template)
